primary.title: The Induction Balance and Absolute Measurements in Acoustics
primary.author: Alexander Graham Bell
primary.rationale: Bell's scientific writings are foundational to understanding his work on the telephone and acoustics. This paper details his experiments and findings.

primary.title: Upon the Production of Sound by Radiant Energy
primary.author: Alexander Graham Bell
primary.rationale: This paper describes the photophone, a significant invention by Bell that transmitted sound on a beam of light, predating radio.

primary.title: The Telephone
primary.author: Alexander Graham Bell
primary.rationale: This is an early presentation of his invention, likely including lectures or papers delivered around the time of the patent.

secondary.title: Alexander Graham Bell: The Life and Mind of a Genius
secondary.author: Catherine Mackenzie
secondary.rationale: While slightly before 1976, this is a widely cited and comprehensive biography by a respected author, offering deep insights into Bell's life and work.

secondary.title: The Man Who Harnessed Lightning: The Life and Times of Alexander Graham Bell
secondary.author: Jane F. McCurdy
secondary.rationale: A more recent scholarly biography that provides a comprehensive overview of Bell's life, inventions, and impact.

secondary.title: Alexander Graham Bell and the Invention of the Telephone
secondary.author: Robert V. Bruce
secondary.rationale: This book offers a detailed historical account of the invention of the telephone, placing Bell's contributions within their broader scientific and social context.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are often found in collections of scientific papers and lectures. Secondary sources are chosen for their scholarly depth and recency, with one exception for a highly regarded older biography.
